name: Direct anterior approach to the hip (periprosthetic)
corridor: Anterior Hueter interval between tensor fasciae latae (superior gluteal nerve) and sartorius/rectus femoris (femoral nerve), through a T-capsulotomy to the femoral head and neck

positioning.text: Position supine on a standard or specialty table with the ipsilateral arm padded across the chest and the limb free for traction and rotation.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark the anterior superior iliac spine and the tensor fasciae latae; the incision runs from just lateral and distal to the ASIS toward the lateral femoral epicondyle over the TFL.

incision.text: Make an approximately 10 cm incision over the tensor fasciae latae, entering the TFL sheath from its medial side to spare the muscle belly.

superficial_interval.text: Develop the Hueter interval between the tensor fasciae latae laterally and the sartorius and rectus femoris medially, keeping the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve protected within the sartorial fascia.

deep_interval.text: Isolate and coagulate the ascending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex vessels, place a retractor around the superior femoral neck, and expose the anterior capsule.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous tissue with the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, TFL sheath, the intermuscular Hueter interval, the lateral femoral circumflex vessels, and the anterior hip capsule.

structures_at_risk.text: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve, the femoral nerve deep to an aggressive medial retractor, and the ascending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex artery are at risk.

danger_zones.text: The medial edge of the interval is the danger zone: branches of the lateral femoral cutaneous nerve that perforate the fascia early, and femoral nerve traction from a deep medial retractor.

retraction_hazards.text: Avoid forceful medial retraction, which can injure the femoral nerve, and protect lateral femoral cutaneous nerve branches in the subcutaneous fat.

exposure.text: A T-shaped capsulotomy with medial and lateral stay sutures exposes the femoral head and neck for arthroplasty or fracture work.

limitations.text: The approach gives restricted access to posterior wall and column fractures and limited femoral exposure without extension.

indications.text: Indicated for primary total hip arthroplasty and for periprosthetic fracture treatment where the posterior capsule is preserved, and it can be extended for fixation.

closure.text: Close the capsule with non-absorbable sutures, close the TFL fascia, and consider a subfascial drain given the bleeding risk from the circumflex vessels.

complications.text: Complications include lateral femoral cutaneous nerve paresthesia, femoral nerve injury, wound problems, and bleeding from the lateral femoral circumflex vessels.

procedure_applications.condition: Total hip arthroplasty is performed through an anterior intermuscular interval
An anterior exposure that preserves the posterior capsule is preferred for a periprosthetic fracture

questions.question: Which intermuscular interval defines the direct anterior approach?
questions.answer: The Hueter interval between tensor fasciae latae and sartorius/rectus femoris.

questions.question: Which cutaneous nerve is characteristically injured in the direct anterior approach?
Which vessels are coagulated during the deep dissection?
questions.answer: The ascending branch of the lateral femoral circumflex vessels.
